body:
When I use the "-h" flag to add missing hydrogens to a molecule in a PDB format (obtained from crystallographic studies):

`$ obabel mol_raw.pdb -O mol_h.pdb -h`

all added hydrogens are labelled identically as "H", e.g.:

```
ATOM     99  H   UNK     1      13.631  10.195  13.948  1.00  0.00           H  
ATOM    100  H   UNK     1      11.411   9.367  14.204  1.00  0.00           H  
ATOM    101  H   UNK     1      11.822   7.829  11.605  1.00  0.00           H  
ATOM    102  H   UNK     1      10.022  10.153  12.336  1.00  0.00           H  
ATOM    103  H   UNK     1      12.365  10.017  10.528  1.00  0.00           H  
ATOM    104  H   UNK     1      10.909  11.602   9.629  1.00  0.00           H  
ATOM    105  H   UNK     1      12.131  12.497  10.503  1.00  0.00           H  
```

Is it possible to automatically mark them with distinct labels, i.e. H1, H2, ... ?

A next question refers to the fact that the atoms from the initial file are introduced with a keyword "HETATM". Then, new hydrogens are introduced with "ATOM" (as shown above), which leads to mixing "HETATM" and "ATOM" lines in a resulting file. May it lead to any future problems?
title: How to add hydrogen atoms with distinct labels?
